title: Why a Windshield Cracks but Holds
coreQuestion: Why does a cracked car windshield stay in one piece?

facts.claim: Laminated glass is a type of safety glass that holds together when shattered.
When it breaks, laminated glass is held in place by an interlayer, typically of polyvinyl butyral, between its layers of glass.
In 1903 the French chemist Édouard Bénédictus dropped a glass flask coated with cellulose nitrate, and it shattered but did not break into pieces.

narration.text: Crack a car windshield and it stays in one piece.
That is because the glass is a sandwich.
Between its layers of glass sits a plastic interlayer, usually polyvinyl butyral.
When the glass breaks, the interlayer holds it in place.
The idea goes back to 1903, when the chemist Édouard Bénédictus dropped a coated glass flask.
It shattered, but it did not break into pieces.
So the layers are there for the moment the glass breaks: it holds together.
